newsitem.title: USA: Loeb collection fetches $92 million at auction.
newsitem.headline: Loeb collection fetches $92 million at auction.

text.p: One of the world's last great art collections still in private hands fetched $92.7 million at auction on Monday, setting a record price for a Toulouse-Lautrec and second highest prices for works by Cezanne and Manet.
The 29 works from the impressionist collection of New York art lovers Wall Street banker John Loeb and his wife Frances, had been expected to go for about $80 million.

Instead, it became the highest total for a single-owner sale in Christie's New York history -- topping the previous record of $85 milion -- since the art market hit its peak before tanking in 1989. Art experts said it was a sign of a new vitality in the market.

The highest price of the night was $23.1 million paid for a Cezanne portrait of his wife. Christie's declined to name the buyer or to say whether "Mrs. Cezanne" remained in private hands. It would only identify the buyer as European. The record for a Cezanne remained at the $28.6 million set in 1993.

The second highest price of the evening was $18.7 million paid for a rare self-portrait by Edouard Manet, which was bought by an anonymous collector. The record for a Manet, however, remained at the $26.4 million set in 1989.
A portrait of a dancer by Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec sold for $14.5 million, breaking the previous record for the artist of $12.9 million.
